slot.brief: Figure shows a disubstituted benzene with one activating and one deactivating group; predict the major mononitration product considering the stronger director.

stem: On mononitration with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ of the compound as shown in the figure, which product is favoured?

verdicts.working: CHO directs nitration meta; methyl directs ortho/para. Both favor positions 3 and 5. Position 5 is less sterically hindered than position 3, so the favoured product is 2-methyl-5-nitrobenzaldehyde.

working:
The methyl group directs to C3 and C5; the aldehyde group directs meta to itself, also to C3 and C5.
C5 is para to methyl, whereas C3 is ortho to methyl.
The less hindered para product is favoured: 2-methyl-5-nitrobenzaldehyde.

Independent check: CHO directs nitration meta; methyl directs ortho/para. Both favor positions 3 and 5. Position 5 is less sterically hindered than position 3, so the favoured product is 2-methyl-5-nitrobenzaldehyde.
solution: The $-CHO$ group directs nitration meta, while $-CH_3$ directs ortho/para; both groups therefore favour substitution at C3 and C5. C5 is para to methyl and less sterically hindered than C3, which is ortho to methyl. Hence the favoured product is 2-methyl-5-nitrobenzaldehyde.

draft.stem: On mononitration with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ of the compound as shown in the figure, which product is favoured?

figure.description: Draw a benzene hexagon with an aldehyde group (–CHO) at vertex 1 and a methyl group (–CH3) at the adjacent vertex 2. Show a reaction arrow pointing right from the substrate, with concentrated HNO3 and concentrated H2SO4 above the arrow. Leave the product side blank.

draft.working:
The methyl group directs to C3 and C5; the aldehyde group directs meta to itself, also to C3 and C5.
C5 is para to methyl, whereas C3 is ortho to methyl.
The less hindered para product is favoured: 2-methyl-5-nitrobenzaldehyde.
draft.distractor_notes: A: Selects the ortho-to-methyl site rather than the less hindered para site.\nB: Places nitro para to the deactivating aldehyde group.\nD: Selects a site ortho to the deactivating aldehyde and meta to methyl.
